reason: The caveat itself is right. The finding is refuted because it is not new and its numbers are wrong. (1) It repeats round 3: research/wf_ideas_v4/round3/scan_hypotheses.json R3S-5 already says 'The high primary-frame FN rate is a selection effect: those are the frames where the secondary drops candidates, i.e. hard frames.' FACTS F-TRN-18 [c9] already says the clip-level data are 'confounded', and LESSONS_draft s4 item 1 already says 'sign unknown'. The only text that reads the FN gap causally is r12p-2's own gain arithmetic in this same scan, so this is a self-correction, not a recheck of an old error. (2) The 'upper bound' is not an upper bound. The +0.0075 uses the clip-level gap (6.43 - 4.16 = 2.27 pp) x 0.331. The within-mixed-clip gap the finding quotes first (10.71 - 3.17 = 7.54 pp) gives 0.331 x 7.54 = 2.5 pp, about 3.3x larger. Both gaps are confounded, so neither bounds anything; +0.0075 is only a naive causal reading. It also rests on 529 edges in 2 clips (44b6_9be80b04 and e28840c6, the all-primary clips). The binomial SE alone is ~1.1 pp, so the 2.27 pp gap is about 2 SE on two clips. (3) The 'lower bound' has no number. The evidence that exists (round 9 recheck: in fallback frames the blend keeps 22% fewer candidates on 44b6 (310 -> 242) and 15% fewer on 6bba) tilts the prior toward guard-off LOSING recall, which is what the guard was built to prevent. (4) The '44b6 >= +0.002' gate is derived from the flawed bound. The 6bba half of the same-sign gate is effectively one clip (ab78413d at 93%), as round 10 already noted. Value and feasibility: 0 on LB and private before the deadline (#37 and #38 share the guard). It is text only, so it is trivially feasible, but it adds nothing the KB does not already hold except the wrong numbers.
fix: Do not add r12p-7 as a new finding. Curator, one line only: in I-222 and LESSONS s4 item 1, cite round 3 R3S-5 ('primary-frame FN 10.71% is a selection effect: the guard fires on frames where the 0.80-weight blend drops >= 10% of candidates, i.e. hard frames'). Add the round 9 counts (the blend keeps 22% / 15% fewer candidates in fallback frames), which make guard-off's expected sign lean negative. In r12p-2 item #3, replace 'if causal ~+0.0075 (44b6) / +0.0009 (6bba)' with 'naive causal readings range from +0.0075 (clip-level gap, 2 clips / 529 edges) to +0.025 (within-mixed-clip gap) on 44b6; both are confounded and bound nothing; sign unknown, prior leans to guard-off hurting'. Keep the post-deadline arms (guard-off / floor 0.8 / weight 0.475 on the 6 named clips plus all 17 44b6 clips). Treat '44b6 >= +0.002' as an arbitrary pre-declared threshold, not one derived from a bound, and state that the 6bba half of the gate is one clip. No finals action and no submission.
realistic_gain: 0 on public/private before 29 Sep: documentation only, and both finals share the guard. After the deadline it is interpretive (shake-up analysis). The sign of any guard-off gain is unknown and leans negative.
